reason: The problem is real and I measured it; the fix as written does not deliver it, which is what decides this. Driven in chromium at ?v=light&state=full, reading each tick's ink box (Range.getBoundingClientRect) against its own .colw centre: at 1440 and at 900/860 all twelve spans are flex:1 1 0 and every visible tick is 0.0px off its column. In the two thinned bands lately.html:303-308 switches the three survivors to display:block; flex:0 0 auto inside a space-between row, and the displacement appears exactly as the seat says: 1140 gives +1.4 / -23.3 / -1.4 (pitch 46.67), 1024 gives +6.3 / -18.5 / -6.3 (pitch 37.00), 792 gives +1.4 / -23.3 / -1.4, 768 gives +2.4 / -22.3 / -2.4 (pitch 44.67), 390 gives +13.2 / -11.6 / -13.2 (pitch 23.17). At 390 '27 Apr' is nearer column 2's centre (10.0px) than column 1's (13.2px), '13 Jul' is nearer column 11 (10.0px) than column 12 (13.2px), and '8 Jun' sits dead on the col6/col7 boundary. So the mechanism the panel killed on the age axis in r1 does survive on the week axis, the behaviour gate does not cover it (interaction-check.mjs:735-754 asserts only one-line-ness and in-card containment for .xaxis; the alignment assertion at :856-885 is scoped to .strip-scale), and this is not a re-file of any closed or refuted item. The seat's own denominators are wrong in the conservative direction - 49px, 47px and 25.7px against measured 46.67, 44.67 and 23.17 - so the true fraction of a pitch is worse than claimed, not better; the offsets themselves are right within 1.6px. What refutes it is the prescription. I applied the seat's exact rule (display:none -> visibility:hidden on the non-survivors, display:block; flex:0 0 auto -> visibility:visible on 1st/7th/last, flex basis left alone) and re-measured. It fixes 1140/792/768, where the box is wider than the label. It does not fix the phone, which is the width the seat calls the damage: at 390 the boxes resolve to 19.17px against 45.5px of nowrap text, and chromium flushes an overflowing line to the start edge rather than centring it, so the ink lands +13.2 / +9.4 / +13.2 - '27 Apr' unchanged, '8 Jun' still 0.41 of a pitch out, and '13 Jul' flipped from -13.2 to +13.2, now sitting past the last column instead of on the boundary before it. Every visible label on the phone is still displaced by roughly half a column after the fix that was sold as removing exactly that. A correct problem with a fix that leaves its own worst case standing is refuted; the corrected one-declaration version is below.
sharpenedFix: Keep the seat's structure and change one more declaration: in the (max-width: 1140px) and (min-width: 901px), (max-width: 792px) block at lately.html:303-308, set `.xaxis span:not(:only-child) { display: flex; justify-content: center; flex: 1 1 0; visibility: hidden; }` and `.xaxis span:not(:only-child):first-child, :nth-child(7), :last-child { visibility: visible; }`. Making the survivor a flex container turns its text into an anonymous flex item whose automatic minimum size is the nowrap text, so justify-content:center overflows it symmetrically instead of flushing it left, and the ink centres on the box - which, at flex:1 1 0, IS the column. Driven with that patch the offset is 0.0px at 1140, 1024, 940, 901, 792, 768, 600, 430, 390, 360 and 320, with no document overflow at any of them. The overhang falls into the hidden neighbours and the card's own padding: worst ink clearance inside .card.hero is 3.8px on the left at 390, 2.6px at 360, 0.9px at 320, and 34-58px on the right at every width because .xaxis already reserves padding-right: var(--gutter). No new colour, weight, metric or structural change; text-align:center on .xaxis span stays for the full-density case and for the solo axis at lately.html:952.
breaks: The seat's class is right - visibly wrong but passable, because the axis is aria-hidden and the chart's spoken line at lately.html:747 names all twelve weeks with their values, and the running week is independently marked by the hatched, open-topped, mask-faded last column plus its right-railed 'N so far'. Not misleading: nothing asserts a falsehood, the pointing is imprecise. What either fix breaks and what must be re-measured: (1) the r1 closure axis-ticks-go-ragged-between-560-and-900 is now guarded by interaction-check.mjs:753, which measures s.getBoundingClientRect() - the flex box, not the ink. Once the label deliberately overflows its box that assertion goes blind, so it must be re-cut to measure a Range over the span's contents, at 1440/1141/1140/1000/901/900/793/792/768/560/430/390 and at 320 where the left clearance is under a pixel. (2) Add the week-axis twin of the age-axis assertion at :856-885 - every visible .xaxis span's ink centre within 4px of its .colw centre - or this class walks back in the next time the thinning band is retuned. (3) Re-run at first-run, where .plot.solo pins .cols to a 57px width and the axis is a single :only-child span the media query deliberately does not touch; confirm the solo tick is untouched. (4) Re-run the audit for leading and the one-line assertion: display:flex on the span changes how the line box is generated, so confirm the tick height stays 16px and identical across all twelve. (5) Check the 901-1140 band against the record-tag and the gridline value labels at .plot right:0 - they sit above the axis so no collision is expected, but the first tick's ink now reaches the card's inner padding at narrow widths and should be eyeballed at 390 against the hero card's left edge.
